summary: Feed s146_double to IDS is degraded: 8.9% duplicate packets (313/3526) and repeated 3.10 Gbps microbursts overloading the 1 Gbps IDS port (310% capacity, 5 intervals), causing wasted processing and likely burst drops/missed detections.

findings.root_cause: Traffic aggregated from multiple SPAN/mirror sources or packet broker ingress ports without deduplication - same packet delivered twice to IDS. 8.9% duplicates exceeds 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU inspecting duplicates, inflates flow/alert counts, risks duplicate alerts and reduces effective detection capacity for real threats.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short window before delivery, eliminating 8.9% waste while preserving full payload for IDS inspection.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts peak at 3.10 Gbps in 1 ms intervals vs 1 Gbps IDS port (310% of capacity). Packet broker is forwarding full aggregate without load-balancing, filtering, or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port buffers overrun and drops packets during bursts; with needs_both_directions and needs_full_payload, drops cause incomplete flows and missed intrusions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple IDS ports/instances via 5-tuple load balancing to keep per-port rate under 1 Gbps, prevent burst drops and preserve flow integrity for detection.
